records.mutation: impose every constraint on both members of the pair so the symmetric equal-unknowns case surfaces early, and add a re-read-what-is-asked guard against reporting the partner value
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 1/8; two rollouts died at the 16384 cap and all eight burned 14k-16.4k tokens. Six failures fixed one reading of the shown number, enumerated its factor pairs, proved a speaker's own value pins the partner, then declared a contradiction and reported a factor their own text had just refuted; two also reported the partner rather than the quantity actually asked for. The single success was the one rollout that reasoned about the symmetric split where both unknowns coincide, a candidate no factor enumeration reaches. The incumbent's intersect-across-live-readings clause never fires because the budget is gone first, so I replaced it with two cheaper levers it has never had together: impose every constraint on both members of the pair so the symmetric case surfaces early, and re-check which quantity is actually requested before reporting.

records.mutation: make the easiest exact instances plus symmetry the primary constructive tool for pinning the requested object, replacing the round-14 magnitude-plausibility check clause
records.subagent_summary: 7 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct in 5.8k-9.1k tokens. The failure reached the correct locus and radius by ~3k tokens, then spot-checked a messy complex root, mis-inverted a purely imaginary reciprocal so its modulus grew instead of shrinking, and spent the remaining 13k tokens re-auditing a sound derivation until the cap with nothing recorded. Rounds 5-14 all tried to bound, reorder or repair that audit loop and every one lost transfer, while the only proposal that ever raised transfer carried concrete constructive machinery. So I make cheap exact instances the primary tool rather than a late check: compute the easiest ones (the real ones, where signs and reciprocals cannot bite), let them plus symmetry pin the object without a large linear system, and anchor the general result to them.

records.mutation: make the wedge caution two-sided (overlap is strictly partial, so neither containment nor zero overlap), replace parameter sampling with a local enters-vs-leaves trade test, and ban the trailing 'is another configuration better' section that eats the write-up
records.subagent_summary: Only 2 of 8 scored. No failure was mathematical: 6 of 8 held the right overlap value inside the first 3-7k of ~52-62k characters, then spent 98-182 rotation re-tests and 45-83 restarts. Four never closed reasoning at all, oscillating between two wrong extremes - that the big square contains the small one entirely, or that tilting could remove overlap - and one explicitly quoted the incumbent's one-sided wedge clause and concluded containment. Two closed reasoning but were truncated inside a trailing optimality-check section that re-litigated rotation instead of reporting. So this revision makes the wedge bound two-sided (overlap is a proper part, so both extremes are wrong), swaps abstract 'don't sample' for a concrete local trade test comparing what enters against what leaves, and forbids the trailing better-configuration section.

records.mutation: name the unbounded/single-use pair as one dead end ending at the piece count, and pin the per-piece cap to the stated degree verbatim by an agreement argument
records.subagent_summary: Fresh 8 rollouts with the incumbent scored 3/8. The failures cluster on two distinct routes that both terminate at the bare piece count: two argued each piece is single-use (one after first declaring the count unbounded because reuse is allowed, then retreating), and both reported m. The other two computed the per-piece cap one below the stated degree and reported m*(d-1). One long rollout truncated while forcing a single piece to step by the common difference. So the incumbent's residual-degree audit is feeding the off-by-one rather than fixing it. The revision names the unbounded-then-single-use trap explicitly as the same dead end, pins the per-piece cap to the degree given verbatim via an agreement argument instead of a subtract-then-degree step, and keeps the shared-affine-target framing that all three successes used.

records.mutation: append artifact-root criterion (a root reproducing given data is a setup artifact) alongside the retained domain check
records.subagent_summary: 7 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct. The lone failure derived both roots of the reduced quadratic, and both were genuinely inside the domain, but it kept only the root that reproduced the two points it had already been handed. That forced a degenerate figure and a zero value, which it then rationalized for thousands of tokens instead of revisiting the other root. Round 11 tested exactly this artifact-root rule and produced the best transfer this hint has seen, but it deleted the out-of-domain clause and train collapsed. So this revision is purely additive: the incumbent is preserved verbatim and the artifact-root criterion is appended as an extra screen alongside the domain check rather than replacing it.

records.mutation: make the position-to-time mapping the centerpiece: forbid rewording a position as a timing, verify orientation on one concrete run, and count the opening steps instead of the closing ones
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 1/8; six rollouts finished early, so length is not the limit. Almost every failure came from one substitution: the asked deepest position was silently reworded as 'whatever was handled last', after which the student priced it as 1/n (or 1/2) by assumed symmetry. The incumbent states the arrival-order fact only in passing and buries it in abstract atom-counting, so it gets skipped. This revision makes the position-to-time mapping the centerpiece: forbid restating a position by timing, assert that the deepest slot is the earliest arrival, demand one concrete instance written in arrival order as a check, and redirect counting to the opening steps rather than the closing ones. It also blocks the degenerate tiny-case loop that stalled two rollouts into the token cap.

records.mutation: make the small-case route survivable: mirror the original condition pattern with a matched count, treat an inconsistent miniature as a miscount to repair rather than a reason to distrust small cases, and read the confirmed list by ratio to expose factorial growth
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling under the incumbent scored 0 of 8, with 7 of 8 hitting the token cap. The hint did get every rollout to try small instances, but each built the miniature wrong -- too many or too few vanishing conditions -- got a contradiction or a value that clashed with its own general form, and then concluded the small case was unlike the stated problem. All of them abandoned the concrete route there and sank the remaining budget into an unclosable symbolic expansion carrying a parameter the conditions never pinned; the two that emitted anything guessed. So the incumbent already commands the right route but leaves the reduction unspecified, and one bad miniature discredits the whole method. The revision specifies how to size and shape the miniature, reframes inconsistency as a miscount to repair, and adds ratio-reading so factorial growth is visible from few entries.

records.mutation: replace exact-fractions clause with untried backward/goal-directed reasoning rule (name target, find the one determining fact, chase only that chain)
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 1 (train saturated at 1.0 for the ninth straight round), so every remaining gain must come from transfer. The rollouts show no strategy or arithmetic failure: the student reaches the value within roughly 2k tokens, then burns 1k-19k more tokens re-litigating which admissible divisor is intended, repeatedly recomputing the same alternatives and asking whether information is missing. Prior rounds already tried scope-labeling, multiply-back, exact-fractions, output-form, case-uniqueness and arithmetic-reliability clauses; all lost transfer ground. So I keep the train-safe opening verbatim and swap the never-exercised exact-arithmetic advice for an untried goal-directed search rule: name the target quantity, ask what single fact determines it, and chase only that chain instead of expanding forward from the givens. That directly attacks the observed forward-exploration rumination and is broadly reusable.

records.mutation: ban the leading-coefficient-comparison opening (not just full expansion) and redirect the abort guard at re-expansion spot-checks, forbidding discard of an already-derived value
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts: 7/8 correct, so the centered recipe works when adopted. The single failure never wrote the centered form at all: it opened with eight general coefficients and a leading-coefficient comparison, then spent all 16384 tokens factoring cubics. Across prior rounds the other recurring loss is the opposite exit: the student derives the pair correctly, then re-expands into standard powers for a numeric spot-check, mis-expands, sees a mismatch, and abandons a value it had already obtained. So this revision makes the ban cover the leading-coefficient opening explicitly (previously only full expansion was banned), and reframes the abort guard around the real trigger: a failed spot-check is an expansion slip and is never grounds to discard a derived value or return to coefficients.

records.mutation: make explicit refutation of the cheap rival (run a second full pass) the required step, and rule that a failed second pass kills order-two outright instead of triggering a trace re-audit
records.subagent_summary: Only 1 of 8 rollouts was correct. Seven failures all collapsed to the same move: the student called the composite a product of disjoint transpositions and read order two off that vocabulary without ever applying the whole process a second time. Three committed to 2, one to a per-size piecewise mess, one to a smaller power, and two burned the token cap re-auditing a single pass looking for a bookkeeping error that was not there. The incumbent already warned that swap-shaped stages need not have period 2, but a warning was not enough; nothing forced a test. The revision replaces the warning with a concrete refutation step: apply the entire process a second time, and treat a non-return as killing order two rather than as evidence the trace is wrong.
